What we know on day 1,665 Warren Murray with Guardian writers and agencies Tue 15 Sep 2026 02.15 BST Last modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 03.18 BST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Ukraine will only halt attacks on Russian energy targets if the enemy does likewise and the US guarantees it, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. secondary_incidents.evidence_excerpt: Map The Lithuanian president, Gitanas Nausėda, said early on Tuesday a drone “that just entered Lithuanian airspace was destroyed by Nato fighter jets”, adding: “With Russia intensifying its aggression against Ukraine, such readiness is vital for our region.” The drone fell near the village of Pratkūnai, about 60 miles (100km) west of the capital, Vilnius, and near the Kaunas reservoir, and had most likely entered the country’s airspace form Belarus, Lithuania’s national crisis management centre

German authorities, meanwhile, were searching for more debris on Tuesday from a drone believed to have crashed on Monday near Lake Steinhude in the Hanover region, a little more than half a mile from the German Bundeswehr’s airbase in Wunstorf.
A ⁠Nato fighter jet shot down a drone in Lithuania shortly after ⁠midnight on Tuesday, ⁠the national crisis management centre said.
The drone, which likely entered from Belarus , ⁠was shot down near Pratkunai village in southern Lithuania, near Kaunas, the second-largest city, ⁠the centre’s spokesperson said.

The centre’s head, Vilmantas Vitkauskas, told LRT public radio the drone had remained in Lithuanian airspace for about 30 minutes and had flown along the outskirts of populated areas before being intercepted.

properties.article_text_excerpt: Lithuanian soldiers secure the area near Pratkunai village, Kaisiadorys district, on Tuesday, where Italian fighter jets shot down a drone early on Tuesday. Photograph: Mindaugas Kulbis/AP View image in fullscreen Lithuanian soldiers secure the area near Pratkunai village, Kaisiadorys district, on Tuesday, where Italian fighter jets shot down a drone early on Tuesday. Photograph: Mindaugas Kulbis/AP Nato Russian warship fires flares at Danish helicopter as Nato jets shoot down drone over Lithuania Ursula von der Leyen says incidents ‘part of broader pattern of Russian aggression and provocation against Europe’ Jon Henley Europe correspondent Tue 15 Sep 2026 11.18 EDT First published on Mon 14 Sep 2026 23.36 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Russian warship fired two emergency flares at a Danish helicopter in the Baltic Sea and an Italian Nato fighter jet shot down a drone carrying an explosive device over Lithuania in what the EU described as “reckless and dangerous” Russian behaviour. Poland also scrambled fighter jets “due to the activity of Russian jet-powered unmanned aerial vehicles conducting strikes on Ukrainian territory”, the day after Polish security forces retrie

secondary_incidents.evidence_excerpt: Map The Lithuanian president, Gitanas Nausėda, said early on Tuesday a drone “that just entered Lithuanian airspace was destroyed by Nato fighter jets”, adding: “With Russia intensifying its aggression against Ukraine, such readiness is vital for our region.” The drone fell near the village of Pratkūnai, about 60 miles (100km) west of the capital, Vilnius, and near the Kaunas reservoir, and had most likely entered the country’s airspace form Belarus, Lithuania’s national crisis management centre

German authorities, meanwhile, were searching for more debris on Tuesday from a drone believed to have crashed on Monday near Lake Steinhude in the Hanover region, a little more than half a mile from the German Bundeswehr’s airbase in Wunstorf.

The centre’s head, Vilmantas Vitkauskas, told LRT public radio the drone had remained in Lithuanian airspace for about 30 minutes and had flown along the outskirts of populated areas before being intercepted.

properties.article_text_excerpt: Two Azerbaijani sailors were killed when a tugboat was struck by drones in the Black Sea on Tuesday, in the latest attack on civilian shipping near the Ukrainian port of Odesa.The Somali-flagged tugboat TEDY, owned by Mert Marine Corporation, was first hit near Odesa before coming under two further drone attacks overnight as it sailed toward the Romanian port of Constanta.Azerbaijan's Foreign Ministry confirmed the deaths of crew members Aslan Aliyev and Asim Gasimov. Two other Azerbaijani sailors, Imran Novruzov and Rauf Aliyev, were hospitalised in the Ukrainian city of Chornomorsk with burn injuries. Six further crew members received treatment at the scene.The vessel carried 10 crew members in total, including Azerbaijani, Turkish, German and Ukrainian nationals.Azerbaijan's Foreign Ministry said it was coordinating with diplomatic missions and relevant authorities and was taking measures to repatriate the injured and carry out procedures relating to the deceased. František and Ondřej Klišík are slowly going mad – or maybe closing in on enlightenment – in a cabin in the Šumava mountains and, extrapolating a short story about the brothers by Aleš Palán, director Miro Remo succumbs productively to the prevailing cabin fever – not only egging these longbeards on in their squabbling and loopy philosophising, but pitching in with his own fabulism and surrealism.
